question: A shopkeeper purchased some material for ₹800, of which 40% was sold at a loss of 10%. To obtain a gain of 12%, the percentage profit on the remaining goods must be:
solution:
Given:

A shopkeeper purchased some material for ₹800, of which 40% was sold at a loss of 10%.

Overall desired profit percentage = 12%

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price - Cost Price × Loss%

Selling Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Gain%

Calculation:

Remaining good = 100 - 40 = 60%

The selling price of the articles that are sold at a loss = (800 - 800 × 10%) × 40%

⇒ 720 × 0.4 = ₹288

Overall desired selling price = 800 + 800 × 12%

⇒ ₹896

Remaining 60% should be sold at = 896 - 288 = ₹608

Let the profit be of Q%.

According to the question,

(800 + 800 × Q%) × 60% = 608

⇒ (800 + 800 × Q%) = 3040/3

⇒ 800 × Q% = 3040/3 - 800

⇒ 800 × Q% = 640/3

⇒ Q% = 4/15

⇒ Q = 400/15

⇒ Q = 26 (2)/(3)%

**∴ To obtain a gain of 12%, the percentage profit on the remaining goods must be 26 (2)/(3) \%**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__** 

The ratio of the materials sold at profit/loss = 40 : 60

⇒ 2 : 3

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/060bf461c44bc48e1f46ca659f4a28d3e5f0a60f8e4b00bc26b0822a684e39d8.png] 

∵ (x - 12)/22 = 2/3

⇒ 3x - 36 = 44

⇒ 3x = 80

⇒ x = 80/3

⇒ x = 26 (2)/(3)%

**Hence, the correct answer is 26 (2)/(3)%**
